Only the real changes

The SDK waits for fonts and images, hides carets and scrollbars and pauses GIFs before it captures. A deterministic pixel diff then separates change from rendering noise.

Learn more
Any file, not just pixels

Upload Markdown, JSON, YAML, HTML, CSS or JavaScript with the CLI and Argos diffs it as text against its baseline, in the same build as your screenshots.

Learn more
ARIA snapshots, diffed like code

Capture the accessibility tree next to the screenshot and catch a renamed heading or a lost landmark even when the pixels don't move.

Learn more

“If Argos fails, it almost always means something visually changed. That signal is incredibly reliable.”

A flaky badge on every change

Every changed test in a build review carries the flakiness Argos measured on your auto-approved builds. Select it to open the test's full history.

Learn more
Ignore noise, keep signal

Ignore a recurring change in one click, or let Argos do it after it comes back enough times. An ignore is scoped to one diff fingerprint, so a new regression still shows up.

Learn more
Debug from the trace

The Argos reporter uploads the Playwright trace and the failure screenshot of every attempt. Replay the failure in Argos, with no artifact to download.

Learn more

“When a Playwright test fails, Argos gives you the screenshot, the diff, and the trace in one place. Debugging starts where the failure happened.”

Or Weis

One command, one URL

argos deploy ./storybook-static uploads the build and prints an immutable URL. Share it with a reviewer or an agent: it always shows that exact build.

Learn more
Preview and production

Pull requests get previews. A merge to your production branch promotes the build to the production domain, or to a custom domain you own.

Learn more
Private previews, public production

Require an Argos login on preview URLs while production stays open, or lock every deployment behind a login on Team plans.
